text:
Let greed urge
along unknown routes
toward sonorous Tethys
and roaring south winds
the pine that inhabited
the pleasant banks
of fortunate Baetis,
dressed in amaranth;
let it safely admire
the delicious fields
of the mighty Ganges,
crowned with fragrances.


You, green and peaceful
bank of the Anauco,
for me more joyful
than the Idalian woods
and the beautiful meadows
of tranquil Paphos,
you will resound continually
with my humble songs;
and when my shadow
upon the fatal boat
visits the solitary valleys
of Erebus,
in your shaded forests
and secluded caves
I shall wander as one day,
perhaps abandoning
the silent bank
of the Stygian lakes.


The sorrowing crowd
of the nearby villages
will summon my manes
with mournful weeping;
and before the sad tomb,
dressed in funeral branches
and fragrant
with Indian perfumes,
Phyllis will say, weeping:
“Here Fabio rests.”


A thousand times fortunate!
But you, unhappy one,
through barbarous nations,
far from your native climate,
may you falter weakly
under the weight of years.
May the bloodthirsty dogs
that Charybdis feeds
on her rough crags
devour your corpse;
nor may the treacherous wife,
girded by other arms,
soothe your ashes
with grief-stricken cries.

translation.title: The Anauco
translation.editorial_note: Classical names and allusions—Tethys, Baetis, Ganges, Paphos, Erebus, and Charybdis—are retained.
